messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALER T: High error rate and latency spike observed on /v1/embeddings. 502s up to 8% for the last 2m. autoscaler churn observed on inference-dedicated-pool-3. Suspected: KV cache growth + continuous batching regressions. Alert ID: INC-20600044
maria: oncall here, looking. dd'ing metrics now — which customer hit?
sam: seeing same. Top symptoms: large KV cache sizes on node g4-12, batch window lowered from 40ms->10ms in last config rollout (deploy 2026-03-15_09:12). Lots of small batches -> KV cache churn -> warmup loops -> HPA scaling spikes.
kevin: yep traces show many prefix keys never evicted, cache size per worker jumped from 120MB -> 1.6GB in ~3m. Continuous batching keeps replaying prefixes so warmup keeps creating new cache entries.
maria: impact: embeddings latency p50 -> 320ms from 80ms, p95 1.2s, some customers seeing timeouts. Elaine can you correlate customer traffic?
elaine: Customer-facing summary: two high-volume customers (AcmeRetail, DocSearch) saw degraded embeddings; support tickets incoming. Notifying CS and reducing SLAs where needed.
jen: any quick mitigation besides rollback? I can attach a patch if we want to cap cache growth at runtime.
sam: immediate plan: 1) revert batching config to previous (safe) commit, 2) raise HPA min replicas to smooth thrash while we stabilize, 3) apply temporary cache TTL/limit to avoid runaway. Revert rollout ID: 2026-03-15_09:12 -> rollback to 2026-03-13_22:03.
maria: assignable? sam do you want to handle rollback, kevin look at cache TTL, jen prepare canary and patch? I'll coordinate comms.
sam: on it. running rollback now. kubectl snippet: ```sh
# rollback batch config
kubectl -n inference set image config/batching-controller batching=registry.redwood.io/batching-controller:20260313-2203
kubectl -n inference rollout status deployment/batching-controller
```
kevin: for TTL I can push a dynconfig toggle (ttl_ms for prefix cache = 300000) to limit growth. Patch: ```yaml
kv_cache:
  max_entries_per_prefix: 1000
  default_ttl_ms: 300000
```
jen: preparing canary deployment for 2 nodes in eu-west1, will enable patch only on canary first. Also setting continuous_batching.enabled=false in canary.
maria: good. I'll bump HPA: set minReplicas=6 for inference-pool-3 while we stabilize. Sam, confirm once rollback finishes and HPA applied.
sam: rollback finished on batching-controller at 2060004456. logs show previous batch_window_ms restored. Applying HPA change: ```sh
kubectl patch hpa inference-pool-3 -n inference --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/minReplicas","value":6}]'
```
sam: HPA patched and minReplicas=6 in effect. Monitoring autoscaler events — should dampen thrash.
kevin: dynconfig toggle pushed to prod at 2060004472. TTL + max_entries set. Will watch cache size graphs.
deploy-bot: Deploy started: canary-patch-2060004444 by jen (canary targets: eu-west1 x2). Link: https://deploys.redwood/2060004444
jen: canary deployed, continuous_batching disabled on canary, cache limits active. Running smoke tests against embeddings and rerank endpoints.
maria: preliminary telemetry: p50 back to ~110ms on canary, p95 ~220ms. Overall cluster p50 trending down. Errors dropped to 0.9% from 8% in 3m.
elaine: CS: notified affected customers, incident page created. Will send interim status: "Mitigation in progress, rolling back batching config and applying cache limit; expect recovery within 15-30m."
sam: autoscaler events showing fewer scale up/down cycles. Cache size per worker trending down: 1.6GB -> 400MB after TTL. Good.
kevin: still seeing some eviction storms on older workers (edge case). I'll add a background compaction job to sweep stale prefixes after 5m. Patch queued.
maria: good call. jen, after canary looks stable, promote patch to prod. Ensure you leave continuous_batching disabled until we have a proper fix.
jen: promoting patch to prod now. deploy-bot: production deploy started: patch-2060004444 -> all inference clusters.
deploy-bot: production deploy succeeded at 2060004508.
maria: monitoring: p50 95ms, p95 180ms, error rate 0.4%. HPA stable. Marking as mitigated. We'll keep monitoring for 1h before close.
elaine: drafting customer update + PS ticket queue triage.
sam: follow-up actions: 1) revert dynconfig TTL-> make a proper rate-limited eviction algorithm, 2) add guardrail in rollout system to block batch_window_ms < 30ms unless flagged, 3) add autoscaler hysteresis config to prevent thrash from short-lived spikes.
kevin: I'll own the eviction algorithm (PR queued). jen will own rollout guardrail. maria will own post-incident review.
maria: filing postmortem stub now, will include timelines, metric charts, and action owners. Thanks everyone for fast response. :heart:
elaine: adding incident to status page and CS notes.
jen: note for postmortem: add a test in the canary suite that simulates high prefix diversity to catch cache blowups.
sam: closing alert in monitoring at 2060004512. If anything spikes we re-open.
maria: closing thread after watch period. postmortem link will be posted to #postmortems when ready. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
